newsitem.title: USA: Nalco sees further cost-cutting gains.
newsitem.headline: Nalco sees further cost-cutting gains.

text.p: Nalco Chemical Co said Thursday it expected further benefits from cost-control programs that helped the company improve its third-quarter financial performance.
"We expect these programs will continue to show good results," said Nalco Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Ted Mooney in a statement

Earlier, Nalco reported third-quarter fully diluted earnings per share from continuing operations increased 16 percent to $0.52 a share from $0.45 in the same period of 1995. Sales rose 11 percent to $343.3 million.

In the third quarter, Nalco's core water and waste-treatment division showed a sales increase of 17 percent. That included sales by recently acquired Diversey Water Technologies, the company said in a statement.
Nalco's process chemicals division recorded a 10 percent increase, with the pulp and paper chemicals group showing strong double-digit sales improvement.

The Latin American division had a sales increase of 17 percent with strong gains in Argentina and Mexico. The Pacific division showed a six percent increase, led by Korea. The Pacific division showed a 17 percent increase excluding amounts in 1995 transferred to a Nalco/Exxon joint venture as of the beginning of this year.
Sales by Nalco's former affiliate in India, which became a majority-owned subsidiary in the fourth quarter of 1995, also contributed to the company's growth in the Pacific region.
The Europe division turned in a three percent increase with strength in the company's pulp and paper group.
Shares of Nalco closed up 1/8 to 35-1/2.
